resources.name: Peer Support Warmline
resources.modeHours: Virtual (6:00 pm – 12:00 am EST, 7 days a week)
resources.description: Warm Line is a confidential and anonymous service for adults in need of a friend with an empathetic ear and was the first program in Canada to offer a peer support telephone, online chat, and text messaging service.  It is operated by peers who have experienced loneliness, isolation and anxiety themselves. The support provided in Warm Line interactions includes goal setting, problem solving and connection with resources.

resources.name: Kids Help Phone
resources.description: Kids Help Phone is Canada’s only 24/7 e-mental health service offering free, multilingual and confidential support to help all young people Feel Out Loud.
resources.contact: Dial 1-800-668-6868                  Text CONNECT to 686868 or 741741 (for adults)
resources.notes: The Kids Help Phone does not have a strict age cutoff.

resources.name: NISA Helpline
resources.modeHours: Virtual (8:00 am - 12:00 am EST, 7 days a week)
resources.description: Nisa Helpline is a confidential, anonymous & FREE 16-hour helpline for Muslim women and girls across North America, with support available in French, Urdu, Arabic, Somali and English!
resources.notes: This resource is restricted to Muslim women/girls. Help in Urdu/French/Somali/Arabic is available from 12pm-4pm EST, 7 days a week.

resources.name: Heads Up Guys
resources.description: HeadsUpGuys is a men’s mental health resource offering practical self-care tips, screening tools, self-guided courses, inspirational recovery stories, an international Therapist Directory, along with guidance on how to support the men in our lives. Our mission is to support men to improve their mental health, reduce their risk of suicide, and inspire them to live healthier lives.
resources.notes: Based in Vancouver BC, but services are accessible globally.

resources.name: Indian Residential Schools Resolution Health Support Program
resources.description: Indian Residential School Support Program provides 24-hour crisis support as well as cultural, emotional, and professional mental health supports for Indian Residential School Survivors, their families, and Intergenerational Survivors.
resources.notes: Applicable to Indian Residential School Survivors, their families, and Intergenerational Survivors, regardless of their status in Canada. Other languages may be available.

resources.name: Black Youth Helpline
resources.modeHours: Virtual (9:00 am - 10:00 pm EST, 7 days a week)
resources.description:
The Black Youth Helpline provides immediate services for Black
youth, and connects individuals with community and clinical resources.
resources.notes: This resource is recommended for black youth.

resources.name: Hope for Wellness
resources.description:
Experienced and culturally competent Help Line counsellors can help if you:
• Want to talk
• Are distressed
• Have strong emotional reactions
• Are triggered by painful memories

resources.name: Brighter Days: An Indigenous Wellness Program
resources.description: An Indigenous Wellness Program supported by Sun Life was developed by Indigenous educators, school counsellors and community program workers to empower First Nations, Inuit, Metis youth with skills, tools and resources to support their well-being. The program is offered to Indigenous youth from six to 29 years old in both audio and video format.
resources.notes: 5+ people needed to book a group session

resources.name: Hope by CAMH
resources.description: Hope by CAMH is a free smartphone app that provides suicide prevention information, tools and crisis resources to support and guide individuals when they are experiencing thoughts of suicide. One of the key features of this app is the ability for individuals to create a personalized suicide safety plan, which can be done in consultation with their healthcare professional, loved one, or someone who they have a trusting relationship with. The Hope by CAMH safety plan can be accessed at any time – especially if an individual is experiencing thoughts of suicide – and it can be updated as their situation changes.
resources.notes: App available on Android and iOS

resources.name: For a Safer Space
resources.description: For A Safer Space is one and only Canadian non-profit organization dedicating to provide accessible, affordable, and affirming mental health care and human rights related advocacy support.

resources.name: Empower Me
resources.description:
Empower Me allows students to connect with qualified counsellors, consultants, and life coaches for a variety of issues. 

As an undergraduate or graduate student, you're entitled to sessions delivered in person, by telephone, or by video-counselling. Confirm if your school offers Empower Me by visiting your wellness services/resources website or centre.
resources.notes: Each University has a specific link: to find the inforamtion for your school, simply search Empower Me along with your school name on Google!

resources.name: Talk Suicide Canada
resources.description: If you are feeling like you have lost hope and are struggling to cope, if you are dealing with thoughts of suicide, or if you are worried about someone else, 9-8-8: Suicide Crisis Helpline is here for you. When you reach out, a trained responder will listen without judgement, provide support and understanding, and can tell you about resources that will help.

resources.name: Trans Lifeline
resources.modeHours:
Virtual
- Mon - Fri: 10:00 am – 6:00 pm EST
resources.description: Trans Lifeline is a grassroots hotline and microgrants 501(c)(3) non-profit organization offering direct emotional and financial support to trans people in crisis – for the trans community, by the trans community.

resources.name: Togetherall
resources.description: Togetherall is an anonymous, online mental health community for people ages 16+, offering peer support, self-help courses, assessments, and resources, with the community monitored by registered mental health professionals.
resources.notes: Free access depends on eligibility.

resources.name: Telus Health
resources.description: Telus Health services and tools help support the mental, physical, and financial health of organizations and their employees.

resources.name: Kid's Help Phone Resources Around Me
resources.description: Resources Around Me allows you to search for resources in your community like Counselling and Mental Health Support, Sexual Health Support, Housing Support, Legal Support, Job Help, and more.

resources.name: Affordable Therapy Network
resources.description: A directory of therapists offering affordable counselling across Canada
resources.notes: Online and virtual options available; free consultations + low cost/sliding scale options available

resources.name: Take Care Community
resources.description: This platform, a collaboration between the National Alliance for Caregiving and the Adira Foundation, provides support to caregivers by offering meaningful resources for caregivers, by caregivers.

resources.name: It Gets Better Canada
resources.description: It Gets Better Canada is a registered charity in Canada that envisions a world where all 2SLGBTQ+ youth are free to live equally and know their worthiness and power as individuals. Its mission is to uplift, empower, and connect 2SLGBTQ+ youth across Canada.

resources.name: LGBT YouthLine Resource Directory
resources.description: YouthLine’s resource directory helps 2SLGBTQ+ and questioning youth find local supports and services across Canada.

resources.name: 2SLGBTQIA+ Community Resource Directory
resources.description: Canada’s national 2SLGBTQI+ community resource directory for 2SLGBTQI+-specific programs, services and supports. Find community resource listings and more from across all 10 provinces and three territories: from St. John’s to Victoria, Iqaluit to Windsor, and everywhere in between

resources.name: Tel Jeunes
resources.description: Phone and text line for youth under 20

resources.name: Suicide action Montréal
resources.description: Crisis phone line for folks considering suicide

resources.name: Tel Aide
resources.description: Listening service for those struggling with mental health issues

resources.name: Ecoute Entraide
resources.description: Listening service + support groups in Montreal

resources.name: Interligne
resources.description: Pour les personnes concernées par la diversité sexuelle et la pluralité des genres.

resources.name: Relief
resources.description: Support groups for those with depression and/or anxiety and/or bipolar disorder

resources.name: McGill Students' Nightline
resources.description: Phoneline for anyone (including outside McGill) looking for someone to talk to

resources.name: Ligne d'écoute et de référence provinciale pour les victimes d'agression à caractère sexuel, leurs proches ou les professionnels de la santé
resources.description: For survivors of sexual violence and closed ones

resources.name: ANEB
resources.description: Phoneline, support groups for people with eating disorders

resources.name: Vent over tea
resources.description: Sessions in a café with an active listener

resources.name: P10
resources.description: P10 is a meeting place and advocate for lesbian, gay, bisexual, intersex, queer, trans, two-spirit, and questioning youth in Montréal, QC that provides a wide range of resources and free services for youth.

resources.name: Centre de prévention du suicide de Québec
Jeunesse J’écoute
resources.description:
Jeunesse J’écoute is a resource that provides wellness support in multiple languages.

Jeunesse J’écoute also provides a number or resources covering a variety of mental health topics.

resources.name: AMI-Québec
resources.description:
Counselling can be an essential part of coping with and recovering from a mental illness, both for the person living with a mental illness and for their loved ones.

AMI-Quebec offers free counselling for caregivers (families and friends of someone living with mental illness). Please click HERE for more information.

Please note: we have support groups for people living with mental health problems and illnesses but we do not offer counselling services for them. Contact the organizations below for counselling for individuals suffering from mental health issues, including art therapy, and counselling for family members. Most offer free services or charge on a sliding scale.

resources.name: 9-8-8 : Ligne d'aide en cas de crise de suicide
resources.description: 9-8-8 is here to provide moments of connection that create hope, support recovery and save lives. We help people connect to their strengths and find new ways to cope, live and thrive. Our vision is a Canada where suicide is prevented because everyone can access help when they need it the most.

resources.name: Ligne d'écoute d'espoir pour le mieux-être
resources.description:
Accessible en tout temps par les Premières Nations, les Inuits et les Métis désirant obtenir du soutien émotionnel, des services d'intervention en cas de crise ou de l'aiguillage vers les services communautaires.

Le soutien est offert en anglais et en français et, sur demande, en cri, en ojibway et en inuktitut.
--
Accessible 24/7 to First Nations, Inuit and Métis people seeking emotional support, crisis intervention or referral to community services.

Support is available in English and French and, upon request, in Cree, Ojibway and Inuktitut.

211 provides a list of organizations in Quebec that offer free, anonymous and confidential telephone services for individuals to share their psychological situtation with another person to break the isolation.

211 offer lines that are general, specified lines (youth, LGBTQ+, seniors, etc) or specific subjet lines (mental health, bereavement, addictions, etc).

resources.name: BYTE
resources.description: BYTE is a “by youth, for youth” organization that focuses on empowering and promoting youth throughout the Yukon and Canada’s north. Our facilitation team travels to communities throughout the Yukon and to some areas of Northern BC and NWT to deliver innovative and relevant workshops to northern youth.

resources.name: CMHA Yukon (Reach Out Support Line)
resources.description: The Reach Out Support Line (ROSL) is a free, volunteer-based, confidential and non-judgemental service. It is here to support individuals who are in crisis and need to talk to someone about their distress or trauma. ROSL operates 24 hours a day, seven days a week with trained volunteers who will listen, support and help callers find options, no matter how big or small the issue.
resources.notes: Emphasis on individuals in Yukon

resources.name: WAYC (Western Arctic Youth Collective)
resources.description: WAYC strives to create opportunities to prepare and support ongoing development to improve the lives of youth ages 18-35 years old. The purpose of this collective is to empower youth to be changemakers by providing a platform of youth-led collaborative initiatives and partnerships in their communities.

resources.name: NWT Helpline (811)
resources.description: NWT Helpline (811) provides free, confidential, 24/7 phone support from registered nurses for mental health, wellness, and addiction concerns. Callers can receive in-the-moment support for concerns such as stress, anxiety, depression, suicidal thoughts, grief, abuse, and substance use, as well as guidance and referrals to appropriate local resources.

resources.name: Kamatsiaqut Nunavut Helpline
resources.description: Kamatsiaqtut Nunavut Helpline provides free, anonymous, and confidential 24/7 telephone support for people experiencing emotional distress, suicidal thoughts, loneliness, anxiety, relationship or family difficulties, substance use concerns, or other challenging situations. Support is provided by trained volunteers.
resources.contact: Dial 867-979-3333 (local Nunavut) or 1-800-265-3333 (outside Iqaluit + residents of Nunavumiut)
resources.notes: Specific for individuals from Nunavut + surrounding areas

resources.name: Foundry
resources.service: Peer-Community Support, Professional, Educational, Resource Directory
resources.modeHours:
Virtual, in-person  
- Mon - Fri: 10:00 am – 9:00 pm
- Sat - Sun: 10:00 am – 6:00 pm
resources.description: Foundry is a province-wide network of integrated health and wellness services for young people ages 12-24 and their families. We bring together multiple services in one place — in person at Foundry centres and virtually through the Foundry BC app — to make it easier for youth to access care, connection and support. Resources include peer support, counselling, workshops, health care access and employment services.

resources.name: Family Smart
resources.language: English (+ other language translations may be available)
resources.description: Our mission is to provide practical help, service navigation, and peer support to families and caring adults to build their connection, knowledge and capacity to support their children’s, youths’ or young adults’ mental health. Resources include family-peer support, workshops, events and various resources/videos.

resources.name: Qmunity
resources.modeHours:
Virtual, in-person  
- Mon - Fri: 10:00 am – 6:00 pm
resources.description: Qmunity is a non-profit organization based in Vancouver, BC that works to improve queer, trans, and Two-Spirit lives. Qmunity provides a safe(r) space for LGBTQ2SAI+ people and their allies to fully self-express themselves while feeling welcome and included. Resources include peer support, counselling, probono legal services, inclusive workshops and events for both youth and seniors.

resources.name: First Nations Health Authority
resources.modeHours:
Virtual (24/7), in-person 
- Mon - Fri: 8:00 am – 4:30 pm
resources.description: First Nations Health Authority (FNHA) provides culturally safe health, mental health, and wellness services for First Nations people in British Columbia, including substance use support, mental health/wellness education, and connections to community resources.

resources.name: Heads Up Guys
resources.description: HeadsUpGuys is a men’s mental health resource offering practical self-care tips, screening tools, self-guided courses, inspirational recovery stories, an international Therapist Directory, along with guidance on how to support the men in our lives. Our mission is to support men to improve their mental health, reduce their risk of suicide, and inspire them to live healthier lives.
resources.notes: Based in Vancouver BC, but services are accessible globally.

resources.name: Kelty Mental Health
resources.modeHours:
Virtual, in-person  
- Mon - Fri: 9:30 am – 5:00 pm
resources.language: English (+ other language translations may be available)
resources.description: Kelty Mental Health Resource Centre is a free provincial resource that helps children, youth, young adults, and their families access mental health and substance use information, peer support, and community services. The centre offers support from trained FamilySmart peer support workers with lived experience, assistance navigating the mental health system, educational resources, webinars, and referrals to treatment and community programs across British Columbia.

resources.name: Blue Wave
resources.description: Blue Wave is a youth mental health program run by the Canadian Mental Health Association BC Division that supports young people experiencing mental health and substance use challenges. It provides mental health education, self-help resources, wellness tools, and the Living Life to the Full for Youth program, which teaches practical coping and wellness skills through eight evidence-based sessions. Blue Wave also offers the Janice Lee Blue Wave Bursary, a post-secondary bursary for BC youth who have experienced significant mental health or substance use challenges.

resources.name: Child and Youth Mental Health (CYMH)
resources.description: Child and Youth Mental Health (CYMH) provides free community-based mental health services for children, youth, and their families across British Columbia. CYMH offers assessment, counselling, treatment planning, crisis response, and family support for a wide range of emotional, behavioural, and mental health concerns. Services are available through a network of 92 intake clinics across BC, helping families access mental health support and connect with additional community resources close to home.
resources.notes: Hours and contact information varies by clinic.

resources.name: HeretoHelp
resources.language: English (+ other language translations may be available)
resources.description: HeretoHelp is a Government Program that provides access to quality information on mental health, mental illness, and substance use problems.

resources.name: Need2
resources.description: Need2 is an online resource that provides suicide prevention education, online support groups, and workshops for youth and adults in BC.

resources.name: Youth in BC
resources.description: YouthinBC is a program under the BC Crisis Centre that connects youth to crisis support services and offers MindFlip, a free mental wellness education program for children and youth.

resources.name: Crisis Centre
resources.language: English, French (+ other language translations may be available)
resources.description: BC Crisis Centre provides free, barrier-free, confidential, and non-judgmental support through 24/7 phone lines and online services. The organization also offers trauma-informed training and education to help build suicide-safe communities.

resources.name: Mindmap
resources.description: MindMapBC is an online database of mental health services and community resources, including counselling, peer support, support groups, and social connection programs. The directory prioritizes services that are 2SLGBTQIA+ affirming, accessible, and low-cost.

resources.name: Alberta Indigenous Virtual Care Clinic
resources.modeHours:
Virtual                                                      - Mon, Tues & Wed: 8:30 am – 8:30 pm
- Thu & Fri: 8:30 am – 4:30 pm
- Sat & Sun: 12:30 pm – 4:30 pm
resources.description: AIVCC provides culturally safe virtual healthcare for Indigenous peoples across Alberta. We focus on access, trust, and clear next steps — from understanding services to booking care. Our team delivers Virtual Doctor Visits, Mental Health Services (adults and adolescents 13+), Family and Community Care and Cancer Screening, with simple pathways and support.

resources.name: Alberta Health Services - Virtual Mental Health
resources.description: Alberta Health Services serves as a hub for virtual mental health and substance use supports available through AHS and community partners.

resources.name: My Kickstand
resources.description: Kickstand Connect provides free virtual mental health, substance use, and peer support services for Albertans ages 11–25, including free online counselling, workshops, and system navigation support.

resources.name: Child, Adolescent, and Family Mental Health (CASA)
resources.description: CASA provides free mental health services for children, youth, and families in Alberta, including assessment, counselling, psychiatric care, and specialized treatment programs for a range of mental health concerns.

resources.name: The Alex
resources.description: The Alex is a Calgary-based community health centre that provides integrated health, mental health, housing, food, and social support services through clinics and community programs. The organization focuses on supporting individuals and families who face barriers to accessing care and resources.

resources.name: Skipping Stone
resources.description: Skipping Stone is a Calgary-based organization that provides affirming support, mental health services, community programs, and resources for Two-Spirit, trans, and gender-diverse people and their families across Alberta.

resources.name: Alberta Mental Health Help Line (811)
resources.language: English (+ other language translations may be available)
resources.description: The Addiction and Mental Health Help Line provides free, confidential 24/7 support, assessment, information, and referrals for Albertans experiencing mental health or substance use concerns. Services are delivered by a multidisciplinary team of health professionals.

resources.name: 211 Alberta
resources.description: 211 is a free, confidential, 24/7 service that connects individuals to government, health, and social services that are available across the province. The service helps individuals who are looking to find the right community or social resource but don’t know where to start.

resources.name: The Caring Place
resources.modeHours:
In-person, virtual                          - Monday 9:00 am – 4:00 pm
- Tuesday 9:00 am – 7:00 pm
- Wednesday 9:00 am – 4:00 pm
- Thursday 9:00 am – 9:00 pm
- Friday 9:00 am – 4:00 pm
resources.description: Foundry is a province-wide network of integrated health and wellness services for young people ages 12-24 and their families. We bring together multiple services in one place — in person at Foundry centres and virtually through the Foundry BC app — to make it easier for youth to access care, connection and support. Resources include peer support, counselling, workshops, health care access and employment services.

resources.name: Healthline 811
resources.description: HealthLine 811 is a confidential, 24-hour health and mental health and addictions advice, education and support telephone line available to the people of Saskatchewan. It is staffed by experienced and specially trained Registered Nurses, Registered Psychiatric Nurses, and Registered Social Workers.

resources.name: Saskatoon Family Services
resources.description: Family Service Saskatoon is a non-profit organization offering counselling, education, and support for individuals, couples, youth, and families. Services include mental health support, relationship and family counselling, parenting resources, and programs addressing family and interpersonal violence.

resources.name: Need2
resources.description: NEED2 is a suicide prevention and mental health organization that provides education, workshops, and support resources for youth and adults. It also offers an online peer support group for people who have lost someone to suicide and a resource library connecting individuals to mental health and crisis supports.

resources.name: Counselling Connect Saskatchewan
resources.description: Counselling Connect Saskatchewan provides free rapid-access counselling for children, youth, adults, and families across the province.  There’s no waitlist and no referral required. Delivered through trusted Family Service agencies across Saskatchewan, this program connects you quickly with trained, registered counsellors.

resources.name: 211 Saskatchewan
resources.description: 211 is a free, confidential, 24/7 service that connects individuals to government, health, and social services that are available across the province. The service helps individuals who are looking to find the right community or social resource but don’t know where to start.

resources.name: Saskatchewan Health Authority
resources.description: The Saskatchewan Health Authority provides publicly funded mental health and addictions services across Saskatchewan, including assessment, counselling, psychiatric care, crisis support, and referrals to community-based services. Support is available through local clinics, hospitals, virtual services, and Mental Health and Addictions intake.

resources.name: Embracing Life Initiative
resources.description: Embracing Life Initiative is a northern Saskatchewan suicide prevention and life-promotion initiative that brings together communities, First Nations and Métis organizations, service agencies, and government partners. It focuses on healthy life promotion, suicide prevention, intervention, and postvention, with a strong emphasis on youth engagement, cultural responsiveness, and community-led solutions.

resources.name: Klinic Community Health
resources.service: Peer-Community Support, Crisis, Resource Directory, Professional, Educational
resources.description: Klinic Community Health is a Manitoba-based community health organization that provides free and confidential medical care, mental health counselling, crisis support, trauma services, and sexual and reproductive health services. It also offers specialized supports for youth, LGBTQ+ and trans individuals, survivors of violence and trauma, and other underserved communities.

resources.name: Manitoba Farm, Rural & Northern Support Services
resources.description: Manitoba Farm, Rural & Northern Support Services (MFRNSS) provides telephone and on-line counselling to farmers, rural and northern Manitobans. We also offer public education, a volunteer training program, and a monthly Suicide Bereavement Support group. The MFRNSS houses a Rural Mental Health Resource Centre with books, videos and articles related to rural, northern, indigenous, and agricultural mental health.

resources.name: Manitoba Métis Federation
resources.description: The Manitoba Métis Federation offers a toll-free Mental Wellness Support Line that provides confidential, culturally appropriate support for Red River Métis Citizens experiencing mental health concerns. MMF also provides information and support related to substance use and addiction, including resources for individuals and families affected by substance use.
resources.notes: Serves Red River Métis Citizens

resources.name: Hope for Wellness Helpline
resources.language: English, French (+ Cree, Ojibway, Inukitut upon request)
resources.description: Hope for Wellness provides 24/7 confidential mental health and emotional support for Indigenous people across Canada. Culturally competent counsellors are available by phone and online chat to talk through distress, challenges, or other concerns and help connect people with additional wellness supports.
resources.notes: Supports in Cree, Ojibway, and Inuktitut are not available 24/7, so you may need to call in to find out the next time that a language-speaker will be available.

resources.name: Crisis Response Centre (Shared Health Manitoba)
resources.description: The Mental Health Crisis Response Centre provides 24/7 support for adults in Winnipeg who are experiencing a mental health crisis. The centre offers crisis assessment, short-term treatment, peer and family support, and connections to mental health, addiction, and community resources.

resources.name: The Link
resources.focusText: Family-caregiver support, substance use, indigenous support
resources.description: The Link supports youth and families across Manitoba with mental health, crisis, addiction, housing, and family services. Support is available through crisis lines, mobile teams, counselling, shelters, and community-based programs designed to help young people and families access support when they need it.

resources.name: NorWest Co-op Community Health
resources.modeHours: In person, virtual                    - Monday to Friday, 11 am – 5 pm
resources.description: Huddle NorWest is a youth-friendly wellness hub that provides free mental health counselling, substance use support, primary health care, employment services, and recreational and wellness programming. Youth can access drop-in counselling, mental health groups, health services, and other supports in one location.

resources.name: 211 Manitoba
resources.language: English and French (+ over 150 language translations)
resources.description: 211 is a free, confidential, 24/7 service that connects individuals to government, health, and social services that are available across the province. The service helps individuals who are looking to find the right community or social resource but don’t know where to start.

resources.name: Manitoba Goverment Resource Hub
resources.description: The Manitoba Mental Health and Addictions website connects Manitobans with mental health, substance use, crisis, and wellness services across the province. It includes information on crisis lines, treatment and recovery services, community supports, and free mental health programs.

resources.name: Distress Centres of Greater Toronto
resources.language: English (+ Mandarin, Cantonese, Spanish, Portuguese, Hindi, Urdu & Punjabi from 10 am - 10 pm Monday to Friday)
resources.description: Distress Centres of Greater Toronto is a service agency dedicated to providing timely emotional support, crisis intervention, and suicide prevention to people in distress. We are a group of well-trained individuals who are no different from you, driven by a strong will to help those in need.
resources.notes: Multilingual lines are availabile Monday to Friday, 10am-10pm.

resources.name: Gerstein Crisis Centre
resources.description: Gerstein Crisis Centre provides community-based crisis support for people experiencing mental health or substance-use crises, including telephone support, mobile response, follow-up, referrals and short-term crisis beds.

resources.name: Good2Talk
resources.service: Crisis, Peer-Community Support, Professional, Resource Directory
resources.language: English, French, Mandarin (+ over 100 language translations)
resources.description: Good2Talk provides 24/7 mental health and well-being support for post-secondary students, including professional counselling, crisis support, peer-to-peer support, and referrals to community or campus resources.

resources.name: Victim Services of Peel
resources.description: Victim Services of Peel provides free, trauma-informed crisis support, counselling, advocacy, and referrals for people affected by crime or traumatic events, including intimate partner violence, sexual violence, and human trafficking.

resources.name: Family Navigation Project (Sunnybrook)
resources.description: Family Navigation Project (Sunnybrook) provides free, personalized guidance to help youth and their families find and access appropriate mental health and addiction services in the Greater Toronto Area. Clinically trained navigators help identify resources, create a plan for care, and support families through referrals and transitions.
resources.notes: FNP does not provide counselling, treatment, diagnosis, or crisis services directly.

resources.name: Help Ahead
resources.modeHours:
Virtual                                                      - Mon to Fri: 9:00 am – 7:00 pm
- Sat: 9:00 am – 5:00 pm
resources.description: Help Ahead provides free navigation and intake support to connect infants, children, youth under 18, and their families in Toronto with appropriate community-based mental health and well-being services. It helps families understand their options, complete assessments, and get referred to programs that fit their needs.

resources.name: TDSB - Culturally Responsive & Relevant Resource List
resources.description: TDSB provides a list of culturally responsive and relevant resources that are availble in the GTA.

resources.name: Youth Diversion
resources.description: Youth Diversion provides support and programs for young people who are at risk of, or already involved with, the justice system. It helps youth address challenges, build life skills, make positive choices, and connect with community supports.

resources.name: Sexual Assault Centre Kingston
resources.description: Sexual Assault Centre Kingston provides free, confidential support for survivors of sexual violence ages 12 and older. Services include 24/7 crisis support, counselling, advocacy, referrals, and support through medical or legal processes.
resources.notes: Specific for the Kingston, Frontenac, Lennox, and Addington regions.

resources.name: Sexual Assault Centre Quinte
resources.description: The Sexual Assault Centre Quinte & District is a feminist organization that provides support to people who have been affected by sexual violence through counselling programs, advocacy, public education and prevention strategies.
resources.notes: Specific for the Quinte district.

resources.name: Children's Mental Health Services (CMHS) Hastings and Prince Edward Counties
resources.modeHours:
In-person, virtual                                                      - Mon to Thurs: 8:30 am – 7 pm
- Fri: 8:30 am – 4:30 pm
resources.description: Children’s Mental Health Services (CMHS) Hastings and Prince Edward Counties provides mental health support for children, youth, and families, including counselling, crisis support, assessments, family support, and help with emotional, behavioural, or social challenges.

resources.name: CMHA Thunder Bay Crisis Response Services
resources.description: CMHA Thunder Bay Crisis Response Services provides 24/7 crisis support for people experiencing mental health or substance-use concerns, including assessment, intervention, referrals, and follow-up.
resources.notes: Specific for Thunder Bay area.

resources.name: Dilico Anishinabek Family Care
resources.description: Dilico Anishinabek Family Care provides walk-in counselling and culturally based mental health, addiction, and family support services for Indigenous and First Nations individuals and families.
resources.notes: Specific to Indigenous and First Nations peoples.

resources.name: Thunder Bay Counseling
resources.description: Thunder Bay Counselling provides professional counselling, psychotherapy, education, and support to people of all ages and backgrounds. Services are confidential and are designed to support positive changes in personal, family, and work life.
resources.notes: Most of the counselling services are no cost. If there is a fee, it will be discussed with you prior to starting the service.

resources.name: Cody's House
resources.focusText: Family-caregiver support, suicide prevention, substance use
resources.description: Cody’s House supports youth mental health and resiliency by helping young people and their families navigate available services and supports. The organization also works to reduce silence around suicide and suicidal ideation by creating safe, consistent opportunities for youth to reach out for help.

resources.name: Barrie Native Friendship Centre
resources.service: Peer-Community Support, Educational, Resource Directory, Professional
resources.description: Barrie Native Friendship Centre provides culturally based programs and supports for Indigenous and Métis individuals and families. Services include health and wellness, children and youth programs, family support, employment and training, cultural programming, and community connection.

resources.name: Youth Services Bureau of Ottawa
resources.service: Crisis, Professional, Resource Directory, Peer-Community Support
resources.description: Youth Services Bureau of Ottawa (YSB) provides supports for youth and families, including mental health counselling, crisis services, housing, employment support, and youth justice programs. YSB also offers a walk-in mental health clinic where youth and families can access same-day counselling support without an appointment.
resources.notes: For walk-in clinic, call 613-562-3004.

resources.name: The Walk-In Counselling Clinic & Counselling Connect
resources.description: The Walk-In Counselling Clinic and Counselling Connect provides free, single-session counselling for individuals, couples, and families through partner agencies across the Ottawa area. No appointment or referral is required, and both in-person walk-in and virtual counselling options are available, with some evening and weekend hours.
resources.notes: Specific hours of operation and languages vary depending on the clinic.

resources.name: EveryMind Mental Health Services
resources.description: EveryMind Mental Health Services provides free, confidential mental health support for infants, children, youth, young adults up to age 25, and families in Peel Region. Services include counselling and therapy, assessments, family support, single-session counselling, intensive treatment, and 24/7 crisis support.
resources.notes: Specific for the Peel region.

resources.name: Catholic Family Services Peel-Dufferin
resources.description: Catholic Family Services Peel-Dufferin (CFSPD) provides counselling and family support for children, youth, adults, couples, and families in Peel and Dufferin. Services address concerns such as stress, anxiety, relationships, parenting, grief, and family conflict, with both in-person and virtual options available.
resources.notes: Specific hours/mode depends on the office. Specific for the Peel or Dufferin County regions.

resources.name: Hope 24/7
resources.description: HOPE 24/7 is a charity organization that provides free, confidential support for people affected by sexual violence, relationship violence, and abuse. Services include crisis counselling, short-term individual counselling, advocacy, referrals, and a 24/7 crisis line for immediate support.

resources.name: Assaulted Women's Helpline and Senior's Safety Line
resources.language: English (+ other language translations may be available)
resources.age: All ages (+ older adults for SSL)
resources.description: Free, confidential 24/7 crisis service for women/seniors experiencing abuse, providing crisis counselling, safety planning, emotional support, information and referrals to other services.
resources.notes: AWH is a resource directed towards women whereas both men and women can access the SSL. Deaf and hard of hearing services are available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

resources.name: Trillium Health Partners - Mental Health and Addiction Services
resources.language: English (+ French may be available in some programs)
resources.description: Trillium Health Partners provides mental health and addiction assessment, treatment, and crisis support, including inpatient and outpatient care, child and youth services, adult mental health care, and specialized addiction services.
resources.notes: Some outpatient programs require a physician referral. Crisis Intervention is available to people registered in the Credit Valley or Mississauga Hospital Emergency Department.

resources.name: Embrave
resources.description: Embrave provides free, confidential support for people experiencing gender-based violence. Services include 24/7 crisis support and emergency shelter, safety planning, advocacy, outreach, and practical support with needs such as housing, legal issues, and immigration.
resources.notes: Services are primarily for women, Two-Spirit, genderqueer, trans, and non-binary people, with or without dependents. Shelter services are available regardless of geographic location.

resources.name: Peel Crisis Capacity Network
resources.modeHours: Virtual                                                      - Mon to Fri: 9:00 am – 5:00 pm
resources.description: Peel Crisis Capacity Network provides crisis assessment, consultation, and short-term support for people with developmental disabilities and/or dual diagnoses. The service helps individuals and families develop crisis plans, access appropriate supports, and connect with community resources.
resources.notes:
The Peel Crisis Capacity Network supports clients that:                       - Have a Developmental Diagnosis and/or Dual Diagnosis
- 11 years of age and older
- Reside in the Peel Region
- Identify as being in crisis

resources.name: Punjabi Community Health Services
resources.language: English (+ Punjabi, Hindi, Urdu, Arabic, Armenian, Dari, Farsi, Tagalog)
resources.description: PCHS provides culturally and linguistically responsive support for mental health, addictions, family concerns, domestic violence, youth, seniors, and newcomers. Services include counselling, case management, settlement support, and community programs.
resources.notes: Available languages varies by program.

resources.name: Associated Youth Services of Peel
resources.language: English, French (+ other language translations available)
resources.description: AYSP provides a range of programs for youth and families, including counselling and mental health support, youth justice services, family programs, and therapeutic or skill-building groups.
resources.notes: Eligibility requirements vary by program.

resources.name: Tangerine Single Session Counselling
resources.modeHours: In-person                                                     - Mon to Thurs: 1:00 pm – 8:00 pm                                                  - Fri: 1:00 pm – 5:00 pm
resources.description: Tangerine provides free, confidential single-session counselling for children and youth under 18 and their parents or caregivers. Sessions focus on immediate concerns and can help with coping strategies, problem-solving, and connecting to additional supports when needed.
resources.notes: Appointment only.

resources.name: The Dam
resources.description: The Dam provides community-based programs for youth, including drop-in spaces, mentorship, recreational activities, leadership opportunities, and supportive relationships with staff and peers.
resources.notes: Hours vary by program and location.

resources.name: Malton Neighbourhood Services
resources.language: English, French (+ other language translations available)
resources.description: MNS provides community-based programs and supports for individuals and families, including settlement services, women’s programs, EarlyON programs, legal and health clinics, seniors’ supports, employment assistance, and access to community resources.

resources.name: Roots Community Services
resources.service: Peer-Community Support, Educational, Professional, Resource Directory
resources.modeHours: In-person, virtual (BAC Support Line 9:00 am - 5:00 pm)
resources.language: English (+ other language translations may be available)
resources.description: Roots Community Services provides culturally responsive counselling, youth and family programs, newcomer and women’s supports, wellness services, and a support line for Black, African, and Caribbean communities.
resources.notes: Primarily serves Black, African, and Caribbean communities; some programs may be open more broadly.

resources.name: Centre for Grief and Healing
resources.modeHours: In-person, virtual                                                     - Mon to Fri: 9:00 am – 5:00 pm
resources.description: The Centre for Grief & Healing provides free grief and bereavement support for individuals and families who have experienced a loss. Services include individual peer support, support groups, workshops, and community programs that help people connect with others and cope with grief.
resources.notes: Many services have age requirements.

resources.name: Family Services of Peel
resources.focusText: Trauma, family-caregiver support, mens mental health, 2SLGBTQIA+ community
resources.language: English, French (+ other language translations available)
resources.description: Family Services of Peel supports individuals and families through counselling and community-based programs that address mental health, relationships, employment, developmental needs, family well-being, men’s wellness, and trauma recovery.

resources.name: Family Transition Place
resources.modeHours: In-person, virtual (24/7)                                               - Mon to Fri: 8:30 am – 4:30 pm
resources.language: English (+ other language translations may be available)
resources.description: Family Transition Place provides shelter, counselling, crisis support, housing assistance, and community programs for people affected by abuse and violence, with a primary focus on women and their children.
resources.contact: Dial 1-800-265-9178 (for support line)                                                            Dial 519-941-4357 (for front desk)
resources.notes: Specific to women and children; only in-person counselling available.

resources.name: Heart House Hospice
resources.modeHours: In-person, virtual                                                       - Mon to Fri: 8:30 am – 4:30 pm
resources.description: Heart House Hospice provides free counselling and support for individuals and families affected by life-limiting illness, caregiving, grief, and bereavement.

resources.name: Peel Addiction Assessment and Referral Centre
resources.modeHours: In-person                                                      - Mon to Fri: 8:30 am – 4:30 pm                                                                                                    - Wed: 12:30 pm – 8:00 pm
resources.language: English (+ other language translations may be available)
resources.description: PAARC provides assessment, counselling, case management, and community support for people experiencing substance use, gambling, gaming, and related concerns, as well as support for families and loved ones.

resources.name: one-Link
resources.modeHours: Virtual                                                      - Mon to Sat 8:30 am – 4:30 pm                                                                                                    - Tues to Thurs: 8:00 am – 8:00 pm
resources.language: English, French (+ other language translations may be available)
resources.description: one-Link helps people access mental health and addiction services by completing an intake, identifying their needs, and connecting them with appropriate programs and community supports.
resources.notes: There may be wait times. Children and adolescents may be referred to the WhereToStart program. Specific for those in the Peel region.

resources.name: WhereToStart
resources.modeHours: Virtual                                                       - Mon to Fri: 9:00 am – 4:30 pm
resources.language: English, French (+ other language translations may be available)
resources.description: WhereToStart.ca helps children, youth, and families access mental health services in Peel by completing an intake, identifying their needs, and connecting them with appropriate counselling, treatment, and community supports.
resources.notes: Specific for those in the Peel region.

resources.name: MIAG Centre for Diverse Women & Families
resources.language: English (+ other language translations may be available)
resources.description: MIAG provides culturally responsive mental health and wellness programs, including counselling, educational workshops, peer support, and community-based activities that promote emotional well-being and reduce stigma. This is an inclusive support meant for people of all ages/backgrounds.
resources.notes: Specific for those in the Peel region.

resources.name: QTBIPOC Sauga
resources.description: QTBIPOC sauga is a grassroots community organization for queer and trans Black, Indigenous, and people of colour connected to Peel Region. It creates community through gatherings, workshops, arts and cultural events, advocacy, and spaces for connection and discussion.
resources.notes: Specific for those in the Peel region.

resources.name: BounceBack Ontario
resources.language: English, French (+ other language translations may be available)
resources.description: BounceBack Ontario is a free cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT)-based program that helps people manage mild to moderate depression, anxiety, stress, and worry through guided self-help materials and telephone coaching.

resources.name: Horizons for Youth
resources.service: Peer-Community Support, Educational, Resource Directory, Professional
resources.description: Horizons for Youth provides shelter and support for youth experiencing homelessness, including housing assistance, case management, meals, life-skills programming, mental health and wellness support, counselling and aftercare.
resources.contact: Dial 416-781-1933                                                  Address: 422 Gilbert Avenue, Toronto, ON M6E 4X3
resources.notes: Shelter intake is offered 24/7, 365 days a year.

resources.name: Muslim Social Services Waterloo Region
resources.modeHours: In-person, virtual                                                       - Mon to Thurs: 9:00 am – 5:00 pm
resources.language: English, Arabic, French, Urdu, Punjabi, Hindi
resources.description: Muslim Social Services Waterloo Region provides culturally responsive counselling and community programs, including youth activities, tutoring, wellness groups, arts programs, and family supports.
resources.notes: Specific for Muslim individuals.

resources.name: The Bridge Youth Resource Centre
resources.modeHours: In-person                                                       - Mon to Fri: 10:00 am – 6:30 pm
resources.description: The Bridge Youth Resource Centre supports youth through drop-in services, housing and employment help, mental health and addiction support, life-skills programming, and access to basic needs such as food, showers, laundry, and computers.

resources.name: LUSO Community Services
resources.modeHours: In-person                                                      - Mon to Fri: 9:00 am – 5:00 pm
resources.language: English (+ other language translations may be available)
resources.description: LUSO Community Services provides community-based programs for children, youth, and families, including newcomer and settlement support, youth programs, family and literacy programs, basic-needs assistance, and community outreach.

resources.name: LGBT YouthLine
resources.modeHours: Virtual                                                      - Sun to Fri: 4:00 pm – 9:30 pm
resources.description: YouthLine offers free and confidential peer support for 2SLGBTQ+ and questioning youth across Ontario through text, chat, and email.

resources.name: AccessMHA
resources.modeHours: Virtual                                                      - Mon to Fri: 8:00 am – 4:00 pm
resources.description: AccessMHA helps people find and connect with mental health, substance use, and addiction services in Eastern Ontario by completing an intake and matching them with appropriate local supports.
resources.notes: Appointment based service.

resources.name: Pathways to Care
resources.description: Pathways to Care’s Connect Me directory helps people find mental health and wellness services for Black children, youth, and families across Ontario.
resources.notes: Specific for Black children, youth, and families.

resources.name: Youth Wellness Hubs
resources.language: English, French (+ other language translations may be available)
resources.description: Youth Wellness Hubs Ontario helps youth find and access mental health, substance use, primary care, education, employment, housing, and other supports through in-person and virtual hubs.
resources.notes: Specific hours depend on location.

resources.name: mindyourmind
resources.description: mindyourmind' provides youth with mental health information, coping tools, interactive resources, and self-help activities to support their well-being.

resources.name: The Health Line
resources.description: The Health Line' is an online directory that helps people find health, community, and social services in Ontario.

resources.name: Tel Jeunes
resources.modeHours: Virtual                                                                - Mon to Sun: 8:00 am – 12:00 am
resources.description: TJ offers Quebec teens confidential access to professional counsellors by phone, text, and chat, along with information and resources about mental health, relationships, substance use, and other youth concerns.
resources.notes: Parents and friends are also welcomed to chat

resources.name: Suicide Prevention Centre of Montreal
resources.description: The Suicide Prevention Centre of Montreal provides free and confidential 24/7 support by phone, text, and chat for people experiencing suicidal thoughts/distress, as well as their loved ones and people grieving a suicide. It also offers suicide prevention resources, training, and workshops for community members and professionals.

resources.name: Tel-Aide Montréal
resources.description: Tel-Aide Montréal provides free and confidential emotional support by phone for people experiencing loneliness, distress, or difficult life situations. Trained volunteers offer a non-judgmental space to talk and be heard.

resources.name: Interligne
resources.description: Interligne provides free and confidential 24/7 support and information for LGBTQ+ people, their loved ones, and professionals. Trained listeners offer emotional support around sexual orientation, gender identity, relationships, mental health, discrimination, and other LGBTQ+ concerns.

resources.name: McGill Students' Nightline
resources.modeHours: Virtual                                                                - Mon to Sun: 6:00 pm – 3:00 am
resources.description: McGill Students’ Nightline offers confidential and anonymous peer support through phone and online chat. Trained student volunteers provide a supportive space to talk through personal concerns, difficult situations, or anything else on your mind.
resources.notes: Although this service is run by McGill students, it is open to those outside the campus community. This is primarily an English service, and presently cannot accept calls in French. A French chatting service is offered every Monday and Wednesday.

resources.name: Face à Face Montreal
resources.modeHours: In-person, virtual                                                                - Mon to Fri (no Wed): 9:00 am – 5:00 pm
resources.description: Face à Face offers confidential active listening and support for people experiencing personal or social difficulties. Trained volunteers and staff provide a space to talk, as well as counselling, referrals and connections to other community resources.

resources.name: Aide aux victimes d’agression sexuelle – CIUSSS (Centre-Sud-de-l’Île-de-Montréal)
resources.description: Aide aux victimes d’agression sexuelle provides support for people who have experienced sexual assault, including medical care, emotional support, information, and referrals to specialized services.

resources.name: Vent Over Tea
resources.description: Vent Over Tea offers free and confidential active listening sessions where trained volunteers provide a non-judgmental space to talk through personal challenges or stress. They also host workshops and community events, provides active listening training, and connect people to additional supports, including caregiver resources.
resources.notes: Appointment based and each client will pay for their own beverage. Age restrictions may apply.

resources.name: Project 10
resources.description: Project 10 provides free and confidential support for 2SLGBTQIA+ youth, including peer support, one-on-one appointments, referrals, harm reduction resources, and help navigating health and social services.
resources.notes: Hours vary by program/service.

resources.name: Relief
resources.description: Relief provides mental health support for people living with anxiety, depression, or bipolar disorder through individual support, self-management workshops, support groups, and practical tools to help manage mental health in daily life.
resources.notes: Individual support sessions are provided by trained mental health workers, but are not meant as a substitute for psychotherapy.

resources.name: Centre de prévention du suicide de Québec (CPSQ)
resources.description: Centre de prévention du suicide de Québec offers support for people experiencing suicidal thoughts or a crisis, as well as for loved ones and people affected by suicide. Services include crisis intervention, follow-up support, bereavement services, and referrals.

resources.name: Good2Talk
resources.service: Crisis, Peer-Community Support, Professional, Resource Directory
resources.language: English, French, Mandarin (+ over 100 language translations)
resources.description: Good2Talk provides 24/7 mental health and well-being support for post-secondary students, including professional counselling, crisis support, peer-to-peer support, and referrals to community or campus resources.
resources.notes: Specifically intended for post-secondary students

resources.name: The Inquiring Mind - Dalhousie University
resources.description: The Inquiring Mind is an interactive mental health workshop that helps students build resilience, recognize signs of distress, support others, and reduce stigma around mental health.
resources.notes: Available to Dalhousie and King's students only.

resources.name: HealthyMindsNS
resources.description: HealthyMindsNS is a suite of online mental health resources, available free to post-secondary students, to complement the mental health supports and services available on campuses.

resources.name: Indigenous Student Centre - Dalhousie University
resources.modeHours: In-person                                                              - Mon to Fri: 9:00 am – 4:00 pm
resources.description: The Indigenous Student Centre offers a supportive environment for students to gather, meet other students, and have access to community/academic supports and services.
resources.notes: Available to Dalhousie and King's students only. Some virtual supports may be available.

resources.name: 211 Nova Scotia
resources.description: 211 Nova Scotia is a free, confidential information and referral service that helps people find community, government, and social supports across Nova Scotia. Trained resource navigators can connect users with services for mental health and addictions, housing, food, financial assistance, healthcare, crisis support, and other needs.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Provincial Mental Health and Addictions Crisis Line
resources.language: English (+ other language translations may be available)
resources.description: The Provincial Mental Health and Addictions Crisis Line provides free, confidential 24/7 support for people experiencing a mental health or addictions crisis in Nova Scotia. Callers can speak with trained crisis staff who offer immediate support and help connect them with appropriate services.

resources.name: 811 Nova Scotia
resources.description: Nova Scotia 811 provides 24/7 health information and support from registered nurses. Callers can discuss health concerns, get advice on what to do next, and receive guidance on where to access appropriate care or services.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Youth Outreach Program
resources.description: The Youth Outreach Program supports vulnerable youth across Nova Scotia through community-based services. Support can include outreach, crisis assistance, service navigation, family support, and help with challenges related to housing, school, relationships, safety, and overall well-being.
resources.notes: Hours and contact information vary by program location.

resources.name: CMHA Nova Scotia Division
resources.description: CMHA Nova Scotia provides community-based mental health support across the province, including peer support, mental health education, resource navigation, and programs related to housing, employment, and suicide prevention.

resources.name: The John Howard Society of Fredericton
resources.description: The John Howard Society of Fredericton provides support for youth, adults, and families dealing with challenges such as mental health concerns, addiction, homelessness, justice involvement, and social isolation. Programs focus on practical support, building life skills, and helping people connect with resources and greater stability.
resources.notes: Some community training programs may charge a fee. All services may not be available in French.

resources.name: Horizon
resources.description: Horizon Health Network provides healthcare services across New Brunswick, including hospital care, primary care, mental health and addictions services, rehabilitation, and community-based programs.
resources.notes: Most standard services are covered under provincial health services; some non-insured services may have fees.

resources.name: Community Addiction and Mental Health Services
resources.service: Crisis, Peer-Community Support, Professional, Resource Directory
resources.description: New Brunswick Addiction and Mental Health Services offers a range of supports to children, youth and adults across NB, including a 24/7 helpline, treatment programs, and short-term individual or group therapy.

resources.name: Atlantic Wellness
resources.description: Atlantic Wellness provides confidential mental health services for youth in southeastern New Brunswick. Services include ongoing individual therapy, group therapy, parent and caregiver support, and wraparound support that connects clients with schools, doctors, and community programs.
resources.notes: Same week appointments are available, but spots are first come, first serve.

resources.name: PEI Mental Health and Addiction Services
resources.modeHours: Virtual                                                              - Mon to Sun: 10:00 am – 10:00 pm
resources.description: PEI Mental Health and Addictions Services provides support for people experiencing mental health or substance use concerns across the province. Services include a mental health and addictions phone line for immediate support, open-access counselling, and access to a patient navigator who can help people find and connect with appropriate services.
resources.contact: Dial 1-833-553-6983 (for immediate help)                                   Dial 902-218-3289 (for service navigator)

resources.name: Farmers Talk
resources.description: FarmersTalk offers a confidential helpline and counselling program for PEI farmers, farm workers, and their families. The service provides emotional support, short-term counselling, and help connecting with additional mental health resources when needed.
resources.notes: Specifically for those in the farming community.

resources.name: Public Safety Calls
resources.description: Public Safety Calls provides free online mental health support for public safety personnel in PEI. It offers self-guided and therapist-supported CBT programs for concerns such as anxiety, depression, trauma, and stress, with virtual therapist support available.
resources.notes: Specifically for current and former public safety personnel in PEI, including firefighters (career and volunteer), law enforcement, paramedics, public safety communications officials, correctional workers, search and rescue personnel, and emergency dispatchers.

resources.name: Bridge the Gapp PEI
resources.language: English (+ French translations may be available)
resources.description: Bridge the gapp is an online mental health and addictions resource for youth and adults in PEI. It provides self-help tools, connects users with local services and community hubs, and offers access to online wellness education programs.

resources.name: CMHA PEI Division
resources.description: CMHA PEI provides community-based mental health support through one-on-one and group peer support, housing programs, family and community support, education, and mental health training. Services focus on recovery, connection, and helping people access the resources they need.

resources.name: Bridge the Gapp NF
resources.language: English (+ French translations may be available)
resources.description: Bridge the Gapp is a online mental health and addictions resource for youth/adults in Newfoundland and Labrador. It provides self-help tools, connects users with local services and additional supports, and offers access to online programs such as BreathingRoom, which provides strategies to manage stress, anxiety, and depression.

resources.name: Lifewise Mental Health Peer Services
resources.modeHours: Virtual                                                              - Mon to Sun: 10:00 am – 12:00 am
resources.description: LifeWise is a peer support service for individuals in NL facing mental health, substance use, or addiction challenges. Services include a peer helpline, individual and group support, and specialized support for perinatal individuals and first responders.

resources.name: 811 Healthline
resources.description: 811 HealthLine provides confidential health advice from registered nurses for residents of Newfoundland and Labrador. Callers can get guidance on physical or mental health concerns, determine appropriate next steps, and receive help finding health services.

resources.name: Doorways
resources.description: Doorways provides free, single-session counselling for mental health and substance use concerns for individuals in NL. Services can be accessed without a referral or appointment, and if further counselling is required, staff will work with clients to provide access to additional services and supports.
resources.notes: Hours and contact information vary by clinic location.

resources.name: 2SLGBTQIA+ Warm Line
resources.description: Planned Parenthood NL’s 2SLGBTQIA+ Warm Line provides peer support by phone, text, and online chat for 2SLGBTQIA+ people in Newfoundland and Labrador who want someone to talk to, emotional support, or help finding relevant resources.
